\section[\texorpdfstring{\kn{ಸಾಸಿವೆ} (sāsive)}{ಸಾಸಿವೆ (sāsive)}]{\kn{ಸಾಸಿವೆ} (sāsive) — mustard seeds}

\label{lesson:KA-C293-sasive}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for messy, then the Kannada for convenient.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಸಾಸಿವೆ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಸಾಸಿವೆ}} — \emph{sāsive} — \textquotedblleft{}mustard seeds\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಸಾಸಿವೆ}} (\emph{sāsive}) is a tadbhava of Sanskrit \emph{sarṣapa}, \textquotedblleft{}mustard seed\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13281), close to Pali \emph{sāsapa}: the \emph{rṣ} became \emph{s} and the \emph{p} became \emph{v}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sāsive}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{sāsive}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for messy, then the Kannada for convenient, then say \emph{sāsive} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೊತ್ತಂಬರಿ}} (\emph{kottambari}) is a tadbhava of Sanskrit \emph{kustumbarī}, \textquotedblleft{}coriander\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3380), close to the reconstructed \emph{*kōstambarī}, \textquotedblleft{}coriander\textquotedblright{}, that CDIAL also gives. \end{cousinweb}
